```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(e1071)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
data <- read.csv('train.csv')
```

# **Step 1 : Cleaning and Preparation**

```{r, echo = FALSE}

# Remplacement des NA textuels par "None" pour signifier l'absence d'information
data$Alley[is.na(data$Alley)] <- "None"
data$BsmtQual[is.na(data$BsmtQual)] <- "None"
data$BsmtCond[is.na(data$BsmtCond)] <- "None"
data$BsmtExposure[is.na(data$BsmtExposure)] <- "None"
data$BsmtFinType1[is.na(data$BsmtFinType1)] <- "None"
data$BsmtFinType2[is.na(data$BsmtFinType2)] <- "None"

data$FireplaceQu[is.na(data$FireplaceQu)] <- "None"
data$GarageType[is.na(data$GarageType)] <- "None"
data$GarageFinish[is.na(data$GarageFinish)] <- "None"

data$GarageQual[is.na(data$GarageQual)] <- "None"
data$GarageCond[is.na(data$GarageCond)] <- "None"
data$Fence[is.na(data$Fence)] <- "None"
data$MiscFeature[is.na(data$MiscFeature)] <- "None"
data$PoolQC[is.na(data$PoolQC)] <- "None"

# on va regarder si nos valeurs sont symétrique ou asymétrique, interpretation : Skewness	Interprétation : 
# ≈ 0	Symétrique
# > 0	Asymétrie à droite
# < 0	Asymétrie à gauche
# > 1 ou < -1	Forte asymétrie
skewness(data$LotFrontage, na.rm = TRUE)


# On obtient une valeur supérieur a 1 donc il ya une forte asymétrie donc on va imputer par médiane

# --- 1. Identifier les colonnes avec des NA ---
colSums(is.na(data))  # te montre combien de NA par colonne

na_before <- colSums(is.na(data))
na_before[na_before > 0]  # affiche seulement les colonnes concernées avant imputation

# il y a les colonnes suivantes à modifier : 
# LotFrontage : Linear feet of street connected to property | on peut faire la médiane | on va faire la médiane donc on ne touche a rien
# MasVnrType : Masonry veneer type | on peut faire le mode ou alors mettre None | il y a bcp de None on applqiue le MODE

mode_value <- names(sort(table(data$MasVnrType), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
mode_value

# MasVnrArea : Masonry veneer area in square feet | C'est un numérique avec 80% de 0 | on va donc mettre le mode (0)


mode_value <- names(sort(table(data$MasVnrArea), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
mode_value

# la valeur la plus fréquente est un 0 donc on va mettre 0 pour MasVnrArea
data$MasVnrArea[is.na(data$MasVnrArea)] <- mode_value

# Electrical : Electrical system | Il y a 1 cas donc on peut supprimer la ligne ou alors regarder les donner et voir la plus utilisé ou mettre mixed

mode_value <- names(sort(table(data$Electrical), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
mode_value
data$Electrical[is.na(data$Electrical)] <- mode_value

# GarageYrBlt : Year garage was built | On peut pas les supprimer il y en as trop, 2005 ressort du lot mais peu, on va faire la méthode par default : médiane

# --- 2. Sélectionner uniquement les colonnes numériques ---
num_cols <- sapply(data, is.numeric)

# --- 3. Remplacer les NA par la médiane dans ces colonnes ---
for (col in names(data)[num_cols]) {
  if (any(is.na(data[[col]]))) {  # s'il y a des NA dans cette colonne
    median_value <- median(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
    data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- median_value
  }
}

na_after <- colSums(is.na(data))
print(na_after[na_after > 0])  # devrait afficher rien du tout (0 NA)


# --- Imputation du mode pour les colonnes catégorielles ---
cat_cols <- !num_cols  # l'inverse des colonnes numériques

for (col in names(data)[cat_cols]) {
  if (any(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
    mode_value <- names(sort(table(data[[col]]), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
    data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- mode_value
  }
}

# --- 4. Vérification ---
colSums(is.na(data))  # doit maintenant afficher que des 0

# Vérifier skewness avant
#library(e1071)
#skewness(data$SalePrice, na.rm = TRUE)

# Visualiser
#hist(data$SalePrice, breaks = 40, main = "SalePrice (raw)")

# Transformer, Prendre le log réduit l’asymétrie, stabilise la variance et aide beaucoup les modèles de régression linéaire.
data$SalePrice_log <- log(data$SalePrice)

# Vérifier après
#skewness(data$SalePrice_log, na.rm = TRUE)
#hist(data$SalePrice_log, breaks = 40, main = "SalePrice (log)")

# On va combiner les surfaces des différents niveaux et du sous-sol
data$TotalSF <- data$TotalBsmtSF + data$X1stFlrSF + data$X2ndFlrSF
hist(data$TotalSF, breaks = 40, main = "Distribution de TotalSF")

cor(data$TotalSF, data$SalePrice, use = "complete.obs")

# Comme SalePrice est également très asymétrique, on applique le log pour le normaliser
data$SalePrice_log <- log(data$SalePrice)
hist(data$SalePrice_log, breaks = 40, main = "Distribution de log(SalePrice)")

# On crée la variable d'âge
data$HouseAge <- data$YrSold - data$YearBuilt
hist(data$HouseAge, breaks = 40, main = "Distribution de HouseAge")

# On crée la variable pour la dernière rénovation
data$RemodAge <- data$YrSold - data$YearRemodAdd
```

```{r, ECHO = FALSE}
data$SaleMonth <- data$MoSold

# Sélectionner toutes les colonnes numériques

numeric_names <- names(data)[numeric_cols]

# Vérifier les colonnes sélectionnées

# On retire la colonne cible "SalePrice" ou "SalePrice_log" du scaling

# Normalisation (centrage-réduction)
```

# **Step 4 : Modélisation et prédiction**

```{r, ECHO = FALSE}
# ---------------------------
# Robust Step 4: use external test.csv safely
# ---------------------------

library(glmnet)
library(randomForest)

# 0) Assure-toi que 'data' (train) est déjà préparé : encodages, TotalSF, HouseAge, SalePrice_log, normalisation partielle non appliquée yet.
# If you already applied scale() to data numeric columns earlier, you must instead capture centers/scales at that time.
# We'll assume here that 'data' is the original cleaned+encoded train BEFORE global scaling step,
# so we can compute centers/scales here and reuse them.

# ---------- LOAD TEST ----------
test <- read.csv("test.csv")

# ---------- DEFINE THE SAME ENCODING MAPS ----------
qual_map <- c("None"=0,"Po"=1,"Fa"=2,"TA"=3,"Gd"=4,"Ex"=5)
bsmt_exposure_map <- c("None"=0,"No"=1,"Mn"=2,"Av"=3,"Gd"=4)
bsmtfin_map <- c("None"=0,"Unf"=1,"LwQ"=2,"Rec"=3,"BLQ"=4,"ALQ"=5,"GLQ"=6)
pool_map <- c("None"=0,"Fa"=1,"TA"=2,"Gd"=3,"Ex"=4)
fence_map <- c("None"=0,"MnWw"=1,"GdWo"=2,"MnPrv"=3,"GdPrv"=4)
functional_map <- c("Sal"=1,"Sev"=2,"Maj2"=3,"Maj1"=4,"Mod"=5,"Min2"=6,"Min1"=7,"Typ"=8)
landslope_map <- c("Sev"=1,"Mod"=2,"Gtl"=3)
paveddrive_map <- c("N"=0,"P"=1,"Y"=2)

# ---------- HELPER: safe map application (returns NA if col absent) ----------
safe_map_apply <- function(df, col, map) {
  if (col %in% names(df)) {
    # cast to character to avoid factor pitfalls
    vals <- as.character(df[[col]])
    # map only known values, unknown become NA
    mapped <- map[vals]
    # if some names not found, mapped will be NA
    return(unname(mapped))
  } else {
    # column missing in test -> return NULL to signal absence
    return(NULL)
  }
}

# ---------- APPLY BASIC CLEANING TO TEST ----------
# Replace textual NA that represent "no feature" (same list as for train)
cols_none <- c("Alley","BsmtQual","BsmtCond","BsmtExposure","BsmtFinType1","BsmtFinType2",
               "FireplaceQu","GarageType","GarageFinish","GarageQual","GarageCond",
               "Fence","MiscFeature","PoolQC")
for (col in cols_none) {
  if (col %in% names(test)) test[[col]][is.na(test[[col]])] <- "None"
}

# Create TotalSF, HouseAge, RemodAge if possible (guard for missing components)
if (all(c("TotalBsmtSF","X1stFlrSF","X2ndFlrSF") %in% names(test))) {
  test$TotalSF <- test$TotalBsmtSF + test$X1stFlrSF + test$X2ndFlrSF
} else {
  # if some components missing, create TotalSF = sum of existing ones (NA -> 0)
  tb <- if("TotalBsmtSF" %in% names(test)) test$TotalBsmtSF else 0
  x1 <- if("X1stFlrSF" %in% names(test)) test$X1stFlrSF else 0
  x2 <- if("X2ndFlrSF" %in% names(test)) test$X2ndFlrSF else 0
  test$TotalSF <- tb + x1 + x2
}

if ("YrSold" %in% names(test) & "YearBuilt" %in% names(test)) {
  test$HouseAge <- test$YrSold - test$YearBuilt
} else {
  test$HouseAge <- NA
}

if ("YrSold" %in% names(test) & "YearRemodAdd" %in% names(test)) {
  test$RemodAge <- test$YrSold - test$YearRemodAdd
} else {
  test$RemodAge <- NA
}

# ---------- ENCODAGE ORDINAL (même logique que pour le train) ----------
# Apply maps only if column exists, otherwise create column with NA
if ("ExterQual" %in% names(test)) test$ExterQual_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$ExterQual)] else test$ExterQual_num <- NA
if ("ExterCond" %in% names(test)) test$ExterCond_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$ExterCond)] else test$ExterCond_num <- NA
if ("BsmtQual" %in% names(test)) test$BsmtQual_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$BsmtQual)] else test$BsmtQual_num <- NA
if ("BsmtCond" %in% names(test)) test$BsmtCond_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$BsmtCond)] else test$BsmtCond_num <- NA
if ("HeatingQC" %in% names(test)) test$HeatingQC_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$HeatingQC)] else test$HeatingQC_num <- NA
if ("KitchenQual" %in% names(test)) test$KitchenQual_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$KitchenQual)] else test$KitchenQual_num <- NA
if ("FireplaceQu" %in% names(test)) test$FireplaceQu_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$FireplaceQu)] else test$FireplaceQu_num <- NA
if ("GarageQual" %in% names(test)) test$GarageQual_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$GarageQual)] else test$GarageQual_num <- NA
if ("GarageCond" %in% names(test)) test$GarageCond_num <- qual_map[as.character(test$GarageCond)] else test$GarageCond_num <- NA

if ("BsmtExposure" %in% names(test)) test$BsmtExposure_num <- bsmt_exposure_map[as.character(test$BsmtExposure)] else test$BsmtExposure_num <- NA
if ("BsmtFinType1" %in% names(test)) test$BsmtFinType1_num <- bsmtfin_map[as.character(test$BsmtFinType1)] else test$BsmtFinType1_num <- NA
if ("BsmtFinType2" %in% names(test)) test$BsmtFinType2_num <- bsmtfin_map[as.character(test$BsmtFinType2)] else test$BsmtFinType2_num <- NA

if ("PoolQC" %in% names(test)) test$PoolQC_num <- pool_map[as.character(test$PoolQC)] else test$PoolQC_num <- NA
if ("Fence" %in% names(test)) test$Fence_num <- fence_map[as.character(test$Fence)] else test$Fence_num <- NA

if ("Functional" %in% names(test)) test$Functional_num <- functional_map[as.character(test$Functional)] else test$Functional_num <- NA
if ("LandSlope" %in% names(test)) test$LandSlope_num <- landslope_map[as.character(test$LandSlope)] else test$LandSlope_num <- NA
if ("PavedDrive" %in% names(test)) test$PavedDrive_num <- paveddrive_map[as.character(test$PavedDrive)] else test$PavedDrive_num <- NA

# ---------- IMPUTE test missing numerics by train medians where necessary ----------
# compute medians from train (data) for all numeric train columns
train_numcols <- sapply(data, is.numeric)
train_numnames <- names(data)[train_numcols]

train_medians <- sapply(data[train_numnames], function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE))

# For each numeric column present in train but missing in test, create it and fill with train median
for (col in train_numnames) {
  if (!(col %in% names(test))) {
    test[[col]] <- train_medians[col]
  } else {
    # if exists but has NA, replace NA by train median
    if (any(is.na(test[[col]]))) test[[col]][is.na(test[[col]])] <- train_medians[col]
  }
}

# ---------- ALIGN test numeric dataframe to train numeric columns ----------
test_num <- test[, train_numnames, drop = FALSE]  # now has same column names as train_numnames

# ---------- NORMALISATION: use train centers and scales (very important) ----------
# Compute centers/scales from train (if you already scaled train earlier, save them then; if not, compute now)
train_means <- sapply(data[train_numnames], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
train_sds   <- sapply(data[train_numnames], sd, na.rm = TRUE)

# Avoid division by zero: where sd == 0 set to 1
train_sds[train_sds == 0] <- 1

# Scale train and test consistently (if train was already scaled earlier, skip scaling train again but still use recorded centers/sds)
train_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(data[train_numnames], center = train_means, scale = train_sds))
test_scaled  <- as.data.frame(scale(test_num, center = train_means, scale = train_sds))

# Replace NA left (just in case) by train median
for (col in names(test_scaled)) {
  if (any(is.na(test_scaled[[col]]))) test_scaled[[col]][is.na(test_scaled[[col]])] <- 0  # after centering 0 = mean
}

# ---------- PREPARE X/Y FOR glmnet ----------
# In train_scaled, the target SalePrice_log must be present
# ensure SalePrice_log exists in train_scaled (it is numeric in train_numnames)
y_train <- train_scaled$SalePrice_log
x_train <- as.matrix(train_scaled[, colnames(train_scaled) != "SalePrice_log"])

# For test, create x_test with the exact same column order
x_test <- as.matrix(test_scaled[, colnames(x_train), drop = FALSE])

# ---------- FIT MODELS ----------
# Linear model on original train (use original data or scaled? We'll use train_scaled for consistency)
lm_formula <- as.formula("SalePrice_log ~ OverallQual + TotalSF + GarageCars + GrLivArea + YearBuilt")
lm_model <- lm(lm_formula, data = data) # OK to use original cleaned data (not scaled) if you prefer

# Predict (linear) - careful: predict expects same variable types; use test (not scaled) for formula-based predict
# If some predictor columns missing in test, create them earlier; we ensured test has these columns (imputed)
pred_lm_log <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test)
pred_lm <- exp(pred_lm_log)  # back to price

# LASSO
# Recréer les matrices X/Y après ajout de features
num_cols <- sapply(data, is.numeric)
train_num <- data[, num_cols]

x_train <- as.matrix(train_num[, colnames(train_num) != "SalePrice_log"])
y_train <- train_num$SalePrice_log

# Validation croisée
set.seed(123)
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 1, nfolds = 10)
plot(lasso_cv)

best_lambda <- lasso_cv$lambda.min
lasso_model <- glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 1, lambda = best_lambda)

# Coefficients sélectionnés
coef(lasso_model)

# Random Forest (fit on train original)
set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  SalePrice_log ~ OverallQual + TotalSF + GarageCars + GrLivArea + YearBuilt,
  data = data,
  ntree = 1000,        # augmente le nombre d’arbres
  mtry = 3,            # variables testées à chaque split (essaie aussi sqrt(p))
  nodesize = 3,        # taille minimale des nœuds feuilles
  importance = TRUE
)
varImpPlot(rf_model)
pred_rf_log <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test)
pred_rf <- exp(pred_rf_log)

# ---------- CHECK RESULTS ----------
cat("Predictions sizes:", length(pred_lm), length(pred_lasso), length(pred_rf), "\n")
head(pred_lm)
head(pred_lasso)
head(pred_rf)

# Optionally write csv for Kaggle: need Id column in test
if ("Id" %in% names(test)) {
  submission <- data.frame(Id = test$Id, SalePrice = pred_rf)  # choose rf or ensemble
  write.csv(submission, "submission_rf.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  cat("submission_rf.csv written\n")
} else {
  cat("No Id column in test, skip writing submission.\n")
}

# 8) ÉVALUATION SUR LE TRAIN

# Prédictions sur le train pour évaluer la précision
pred_train_lm <- predict(lm_model, newdata = data)
pred_train_rf <- predict(rf_model, newdata = data)
pred_train_lasso <- predict(lasso_cv, s = best_lambda, newx = x_train)

# Revenir sur l'échelle réelle
pred_train_lm_real <- exp(pred_train_lm)
pred_train_rf_real <- exp(pred_train_rf)
pred_train_lasso_real <- exp(pred_train_lasso)

# Vraies valeurs
real_values <- data$SalePrice

# Fonctions de mesure
rmse <- function(pred, real) sqrt(mean((pred - real)^2))
mae <- function(pred, real) mean(abs(pred - real))
r2 <- function(pred, real) cor(pred, real)^2

# Calcul des scores
results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Linear Regression", "Random Forest", "LASSO"),
  RMSE = c(rmse(pred_train_lm_real, real_values),
           rmse(pred_train_rf_real, real_values),
           rmse(pred_train_lasso_real, real_values)),
  MAE = c(mae(pred_train_lm_real, real_values),
          mae(pred_train_rf_real, real_values),
          mae(pred_train_lasso_real, real_values)),
  R2 = c(r2(pred_train_lm_real, real_values),
         r2(pred_train_rf_real, real_values),
         r2(pred_train_lasso_real, real_values))
)

print(results)

# Visualisation des performances
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(results, aes(x = Model, y = RMSE, fill = Model)) +
```
